whatItIs.text: Vinegar brewed from rice wine across East Asia — mild and mellow in Japan (about 5% acetic acid), stronger and more varied in China, essential to sushi rice.

historyNote.text: Edomae-style sushi was traditionally seasoned with akazu, a red rice vinegar made from sake lees aged up to twenty years; in Japan, sake brewer Matazaemon Nakano discovered rice vinegar could be made from sake lees, founding what became the Mizkan company.

howToChoose.text: 'Seasoned' rice vinegar already has sugar and salt (that is the sushi one); for dressings and pickles choose unseasoned so you control the seasoning.

storage.text: Keep sealed in a cool, dark cupboard.

useItUp.text: Splash it over cucumber salads, into quick pickles, or over hot rice with a spoon of sugar for DIY sushi seasoning; it also brightens noodle sauces and slaws.

substitutions.note: sharper; add a pinch of sugar
